newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar ignores October trade data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar ignores October trade data.

text.p: The Singapore dollar remained unmoved by data showing the city-state's exports in October were up slightly after sharp falls the previous two months, dealers said on Wednesday.
"There was no reaction. Nothing at all," said a European bank dealer. The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4005/12 to the U.S. dollar at 0705 GMT against its opening 1.3998/4008.
Singapore's non-oil domestic exports rose a nominal 1.1 percent year-on-year in October after falling 6.2 percent in September, the Trade Development Board said.
Economists said the rise in exports could signal that Singapore's export slump had bottomed out.
The weakness in exports has been largely attributed to a slowdown in the electronics industry in the United States and Japan.
